Accuracy rises slowly with total steps, about 0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch (1.5–2.7 s/pp). The E036 tip scored 5.31 s and 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Fresh seeds 13–22 gave 0.7525, so the population mean is about 0.752–0.753, only 0.2–0.3 pp above the 0.75 bar. The tip sits at the accuracy cliff.

Mechanisms and evidence:
1. Early low resolution is cheap (E026, E033). E040 and E041 each saved 0.1–0.17 s but cost 0.07–0.2 pp. The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
2. Backward truncation saves more time than its MAC share (E028, E034, E036). The dose is nonlinear: E037's 60% freeze cost about 0.4 pp. E042's partial freeze read 0.7549 at 5.27 s, which is noise-compatible with neutral. E039's BN fold is not worth it.
3. Averaging, LS, warm-up and Lookahead-interval tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032) are null or negative. The recipe is at a narrow local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by about −0.1 pp. BN recalibration (E044) read −0.1 pp on seeds 0–2 against the paired design. It is not clearly helpful.
4. wd ×0.5 helped about 0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw (E006).
5. Systems-only work is worth about 1–2% each. Math-identical changes keep per-seed outcomes bit-identical (E035).
6. Sample dropping (E031) costs about 0.3 pp for about 0.5 s, which is no better than the epoch dial.
7. Any change to the RNG stream or step count re-rolls seeds 0–2, with scatter SE about 0.12 pp. E043 and E038 were no-change runs of the same commit, and they read 0.7497 and 0.7525 against 0.7532. So either the harness is not bit-reproducible or the 3-seed noise is about 0.2 pp. I treat 3-seed noise as about 0.15–0.2 pp.

Noise: time ±0.03 s. 10-seed SE is about 0.06 pp. Seeds 3–12 carry a winner's curse of about 0.1–0.2 pp.

Misses: the times of E034, E037 and E041 (the savings were larger than I modelled), E037's accuracy cliff, E042's accuracy (better than I predicted), and E043's accuracy drift on an identical recipe. Lesson: widen the accuracy ranges to about ±0.3 pp. Time savings from truncating steps are nonlinear and tend to exceed the model.

Simplest model: time ≈ 0.1 s fixed + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost has a pixel-proportional compute part plus a large bandwidth-bound part on the 31×31 stem maps. Accuracy rises slowly with total steps, about 0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch (1.5–2.7 s/pp). The E036 tip scored 5.31 s and 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Fresh seeds 13–22 gave 0.7525, so the population mean is about 0.752–0.753, only 0.2–0.3 pp above the 0.75 bar. The tip sits at the accuracy cliff.

Mechanisms and evidence:
1. Early low resolution is cheap (E026, E033). E040 and E041 each saved 0.1–0.17 s but cost 0.07–0.2 pp. The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
2. Backward truncation saves more time than its MAC share (E028, E034, E036). The dose is nonlinear: E037's 60% freeze cost about 0.4 pp. E042's partial freeze read 0.7549 at 5.27 s, which is noise-compatible with neutral. E039's BN fold is not worth it.
3. Averaging, LS, warm-up and Lookahead-interval tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032) are null or negative. The recipe is at a narrow local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by about −0.1 pp. BN recalibration (E044) read −0.1 pp on seeds 0–2 against the paired design. It is not clearly helpful.
4. wd ×0.5 helped about 0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw (E006).
5. Systems-only work is worth about 1–2% each. Math-identical changes keep per-seed outcomes bit-identical (E035).
6. Sample dropping (E031) costs about 0.3 pp for about 0.5 s, which is no better than the epoch dial.
7. Any change to the RNG stream or step count re-rolls seeds 0–2, with scatter SE about 0.12 pp. E043 and E038 were no-change runs of the same commit, and they read 0.7497 and 0.7525 against 0.7532. So either the harness is not bit-reproducible or the 3-seed noise is about 0.2 pp. I treat 3-seed noise as about 0.15–0.2 pp.

Noise: time ±0.03 s. 10-seed SE is about 0.06 pp. Seeds 3–12 carry a winner's curse of about 0.1–0.2 pp.

Misses: the times of E034, E037 and E041 (the savings were larger than I modelled), E037's accuracy cliff, E042's accuracy (better than I predicted), and E043's accuracy drift on an identical recipe. Lesson: widen the accuracy ranges to about ±0.3 pp. Time savings from truncating steps are nonlinear and tend to exceed the model.

Unsure: the true tip mean; whether bandwidth-bound levers transfer to the PCIe judge; where the stem inefficiency lives; and whether a smaller batch buys accuracy cheaply.

forecasts.reason: Doubling the steps in the 20 px phase adds launch overhead, so time rises. The accuracy gain is plausible but small and within noise.
Freezing group 2 for the last 10% saves about 1.5%, but the accuracy cost is uncertain given E037's cliff.
The profile will likely show conv1 and the stem are bandwidth-heavy. Time and accuracy are the same as the tip, up to noise.
A 5% drop saves about 0.12 s and costs about 0.1–0.15 pp, which is the same rate as the dial.
The math is identical, so accuracy is unchanged up to a re-roll. Padding the channels to 32 may give 0–2%.

cruxes: What is the tip's true population mean on unselected seeds? A mean of 0.752 or lower leaves no room for any further time cut, so only accuracy-neutral systems work survives.
Does the profile show the stem (conv1 at Cin=24 on 31×31 maps) is inefficient? If it is, the padding idea I073 is worth about 2–4%.
Is the harness bit-reproducible run to run? E043 and E038 differ from E036 on the same commit, and that sets how much a 3-seed gate is worth.
